---
title: "Bash"
subtitle: "Cheat sheet for appendix C (and every lesson)"
---

## Where you are

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Which folder am I in? | `pwd` |
| Go to a folder / your home / one up | `cd FOLDER`, `cd ~`, `cd ..` |
| List files, with details, with hidden files | `ls`, `ls -l`, `ls -a` |
| Make a folder (and the ones above it) | `mkdir -p FOLDER` |

## Files

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Print a whole file / scroll through it (`q` quits) | `cat FILE`, `less FILE` |
| First or last lines | `head -n 2 FILE`, `tail -n 1 FILE` |
| From line 2 on (skip a header) | `tail -n +2 FILE` |
| Count lines | `wc -l FILE` (just the number: `wc -l < FILE`) |
| Copy, move or rename | `cp FROM TO`, `mv FROM TO` |
| Delete a file / a folder and all in it (no undo) | `rm FILE`, `rm -r FOLDER` |
| The file name without folder and ending | `basename data/SRR2584863.fastq .fastq` |

## Find and select

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Lines that contain a word / count them / the others | `grep WORD FILE`, `grep -c WORD FILE`, `grep -v WORD FILE` |
| Columns of a tab-separated file | `cut -f 1,3 FILE` |
| Sort, by column 3 as numbers | `sort FILE`, `sort -k3,3n FILE` |
| Count identical neighbouring lines | `sort FILE`, then `uniq -c` |
| All files with an ending | `data/*.fastq` (a wildcard) |

## Redirection and pipes

```{.bash}
echo "text" > FILE        # write to FILE (replaces it)
echo "more" >> FILE       # add to the end of FILE
cut -f 6 samples.tsv | tail -n +2 | sort | uniq -c    # | passes output on
```

## Variables, loops, scripts

```{.bash}
f=data/SRR2584863.fastq             # no spaces around =
echo "$f has $(( $(wc -l < "$f") / 4 )) reads"   # "$f", $(command), $((arithmetic))

for f in data/*.fastq; do
    echo "$f"
done
```

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Run a script | `bash script.sh ARGUMENTS` |
| Make it runnable by name, then run it | `chmod +x script.sh`, then `./script.sh` |
| Check a script for common mistakes | `pixi exec shellcheck script.sh` |

A script starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and `set -euo pipefail`; `"$@"` is
the list of its arguments. See [appendix C, section 8](../pages/C-bash.qmd#your-first-script).

## Permissions

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| See them (`r`ead, `w`rite, e`x`ecute) | `ls -l FILE` |
| Make files read-only / writable again | `chmod a-w FILE`, `chmod u+w FILE` |

## Keys

| Key | What it does |
|------------|------------------------|
| `Tab` | complete a file or command name |
| `↑` / `↓` | earlier commands |
| `Ctrl-C` | stop the running command, or abandon the line |
| `q` | leave `less` or `man` |

## Official cheat sheets and references

Bash has no official cheat sheet. The official reference, and the summaries
the shell tutorials keep:

- *GNU Bash Reference Manual*, the official manual: <https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/>
- In the terminal, `man COMMAND` (for example `man ls`) shows a command's own manual.
- Software Carpentry, *The Unix Shell*, one-page summary of its commands: <https://swcarpentry.github.io/shell-novice/reference.html>
- ShellCheck, the script checker used above: <https://www.shellcheck.net/>
